newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY 96 FARM EXPORTS SEEN AT $3BLN - MINISTRY.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY 96 FARM EXPORTS SEEN AT $3BLN - MINISTRY.

text.p: Hungary's 1996 agricultural exports are likely match the 1995 figure of $3 billion and could rise next year to as much as $3.2 billion, a senior Agriculture Ministry official said on Friday.
Secretary of State Zoltan Kis told a news conference that Hungary's agricultural output was likely to grow faster in 1996 and 1997 than the gross domestic product (GDP).

He said that he expected agricultural output to increase by some 2.5 percent this year and by three to 3.5 percent in 1997, compared with an up-to-one-percent GDP growth in 1996 and next year's GDP target of two to three percent.
"At the same time, the quality of the products is improving," he added.
In 1995, agricultural output rose by 1.5 percent, the same as the GDP growth, Kis said.

He said a likely revival of domestic consumption would limit agricultural exports next year as the government projected that real wages would maintain their real value in 1997 after a 15 percent slump in the past two years.
Domestic consumption of agricultural products was likely to increase some five percent in 1997, following a total drop of more than 30 percent in the past six years, Kis said.

Importers of foreign goods to Hungary would probably also benefit from the increase in domestic consumption, partly because Hungary would abolish its six percent import surcharge by July 1, and reduce its customs duties according to its agreement with the World Trade Organisation, he said.

As imports become cheaper, the inflow of foreign goods would probably increase, putting pressure on Hungary's agricultural trade balance, which is likely to post a surplus of $2 billion in 1996, unchanged from 1995, Kis said.
"I would be very glad if we could preserve this amount (of surplus) in 1997," he added.
